communities.title: Antares
communities.body: FIRST Robotics Competition Team 6962. Founded in 2018, we design, build, program and drive a new competition robot every year. Students run the team: they make the engineering calls, manage the budget, find the sponsors and teach the next group.

communities.title: Khan Lab School
communities.body: A nonprofit TK-12 school founded in 2014 by Sal Khan to put mastery-based, student-directed learning into practice. Approximately 310 students across two Silicon Valley campuses. Antares is the school's engineering program with real deadlines and a public scoreboard.

communities.title: FIRST Robotics Competition
communities.body: Every January, FIRST unveils a new game. Teams get eight weeks to build a 120-pound robot, then compete in alliances of 3 vs 3. Over 93,000 students competed in FRC in 2025, and more than 200 Fortune 500 companies sponsor the program.

matchPhases.title: Autonomous
matchPhases.body: For the first 15 seconds the robot runs student-written code with no driver input.

matchPhases.title: Driver control
matchPhases.body: Students take the controls, maneuver the field and coordinate with two alliance partners.

matchPhases.title: Endgame
matchPhases.body: Robots score points on that season's tasks and race for an endgame position. The higher alliance score wins.

leadershipLadder.title: Join in middle school
leadershipLadder.body: 6th graders start alongside experienced teammates instead of waiting for high school.

leadershipLadder.title: Learn the craft
leadershipLadder.body: Structured training in design, build, electrical, code, fabrication, marketing, business and outreach.

leadershipLadder.title: Lead a direction
leadershipLadder.body: Students own a subsystem, a budget line or an outreach program, with mentors as coaches.

leadershipLadder.title: Teach it forward
leadershipLadder.body: Leads train the students behind them, so expertise stays on the team when they graduate.

schoolTimeline.body: Sal Khan began tutoring his cousin remotely, which grew into Khan Academy, the nonprofit known for free online lessons and mastery learning.
His book The One World Schoolhouse proposed a student-centered, mastery-based model for K-12 education.
He founded Khan Lab School in Mountain View to test and refine those ideas in an actual school.
KLS serves approximately 310 TK-12 students on two Silicon Valley campuses, with an emphasis on student agency and real-world application.

subteams.name: Design
subteams.body: CAD the robot in Onshape, argue the tradeoffs, and own the geometry that everything else depends on.

subteams.name: Build
subteams.body: Cut, drill, tap and assemble. Turn a model into a machine that survives a competition weekend.

subteams.name: Electrical
subteams.body: Power distribution, motor controllers, sensors and the wiring discipline that keeps a robot alive.

subteams.name: Code
subteams.body: Java on the roboRIO: autonomous routines, driver controls, vision and the control loops between them.

subteams.name: Fabrication
subteams.body: CAM in Fusion 360 and the Shopbot CNC router that cuts our custom parts.

subteams.name: Marketing
subteams.body: Social media, merchandise, photography and the team's public voice.

subteams.name: Business
subteams.body: Budgeting, sponsor research, pitching and the partnerships that fund the season.

subteams.name: Outreach
subteams.body: Events that bring robotics to younger students and the wider community.
